expert_term.en: expert heard on rules of experience requiring special knowledge and their application to the facts; nominated by a party or by the court of its own motion

appointment.summary_en: The parties must obtain the necessary evidence, but the court always has the right to obtain an expert opinion on its own motion regardless of the nature of the case (17:7). Experts may be nominated by a party or by the court; fee liability follows the nominator, and the private parties are jointly liable for a court-nominated expert's fee (17:66). The decision to obtain an expert opinion is taken during preparation where needed to have all evidence available at the main hearing (5:25). The duty to act as an expert is regulated separately (17:9). Experts are heard on rules of experience requiring special knowledge and on their application to the facts of the case (17:34).

questions.summary_en: The subject matter of expert evidence is defined by 17:34 (rules of experience requiring special knowledge and their application). Chapter 17 contains no express rule on who formulates the questions or on the expert declining questions outside the expertise or reporting unasked facts (not found). The expert must be heard orally if needed to remove ambiguities, gaps or contradictions in the statement, if the court finds it necessary for another reason, or if a party requests it and the hearing is not manifestly pointless (17:36(2)); examination follows 17:49 and 17:48(3)-(6).

rights_duties.summary_en: The expert must be known as honest and skilled in the field; a person whose relationship to the case or a party endangers impartiality may not act as expert (17:35). Before oral examination the presiding judge checks identity and obstacles to the assurance (17:43); the expert gives the statutory assurance (17:45) and is reminded of the duty of truth and the importance of the assurance (17:46). Right to reasonable fee and necessary costs, and to an advance (17:66).

appointment.summary_en: Chapter 17 applies to criminal cases. In criminal cases the court may obtain evidence only if it is likely not to support the charge, but it always has the right to obtain an expert opinion on its own motion (17:7). The prosecutor and the defence may nominate experts. 17:37 governs court-ordered examination of the defendant's mental state.

liability.summary_en: A witness or expert before a court, or another person before a court under oath or assurance, who gives false information in the case or without lawful reason conceals a relevant fact: imprisonment up to three years. Also applies to hearings by video link or other remote means under OK 17:52 or 17:56.

liability.summary_en: Aggravated false statement in court (serious danger of an innocent person being convicted or of a seriously harmful wrong decision, a particularly significant fact, or particular planning, and aggravated as a whole): imprisonment from four months to six years.

A witness or expert in court (or a person under oath or assurance in court or comparable proceedings) who negligently gives false information or conceals a relevant fact: fine or imprisonment up to six months.
